$comment: ★ TF-C111 (D-FFI-PE-CRT-UCRT-MIGRATION P3): `library.pe` is now ucrtbase.dll — moved with the whole co-state group (malloc/stdlib/string/stdio/io/errno/direct/process/sys-stat in ONE commit). Membership is real and not incidental: `_beginthreadex` spins up a thread that INHERITS the creating runtime's per-thread CRT state, and `_endthreadex` tears down THAT runtime's per-thread block — a thread begun on one CRT and ended on the other leaks the first's TLS record and frees a block the second never allocated. All 4 symbols re-MEASURED as ucrtbase exports at TF-C111 (`objdump -p`); no renames were needed, and the msvcrt dumpbin ordinals quoted below are retained as the c98 provenance record, NOT as the current binding. | Neutral shipped <process.h> (Microsoft CRT) — c98 (Windows-host sub-arc, the 3-header F001A batch). sqlite3.c's SQLITE_OS_WIN_THREADS block (#include <process.h> ~35886) spawns worker threads via `_beginthreadex(0,0,sqlite3ThreadProc,p,0,&p->id)` and terminates them via `_endthreadex(0)` — the ONLY two symbols the amalgamation uses; `_beginthread`/`_endthread` ship as the obviously-paired non-ex siblings (same vocabulary, trivial). `availableObjectFormats:[pe]` — a Microsoft-CRT header is meaningless on elf/macho (a reference there fails loud, mirroring windows.json). `library:{pe:msvcrt.dll}` — all four are msvcrt.dll exports (verified via dumpbin /exports C:/Windows/System32/msvcrt.dll: _beginthread ord 198, _beginthreadex 199, _endthread 268, _endthreadex 269), NOT kernel32. SIGNATURES (Microsoft SDK corecrt_startup/process.h, x64): `uintptr_t _beginthreadex(void *security, unsigned stack_size, unsigned (__stdcall *start_address)(void*), void *arglist, unsigned initflag, unsigned *thrdaddr)` — uintptr_t is u64 on x64 (sqlite casts the result to void*, so a 32-bit return would truncate the thread HANDLE); the thread-proc param is `unsigned(__stdcall*)(void*)` and `__stdcall` ERASES on pe (c95, MS x64 has one calling convention), so the fn-ptr type spells plainly as ptr<fn(ptr<void>) -> u32> — exactly the type sqlite3ThreadProc decays to. `void _endthreadex(unsigned retval)`. `uintptr_t _beginthread(void (__cdecl *start_address)(void*), unsigned stack_size, void *arglist)`; `void _endthread(void)`. The `security` param is `void*` per the UCRT prototype (sqlite passes literal 0). | ★★★ LANE-CFG: `getpid` — the ONE name mingw's `<unistd.h>` re-exports from HERE, and the reason `<unistd.h>` can open on pe as a real re-export rather than an assertion. ✔MEASURED against the same-platform oracle `C:/Strawberry/c/bin/x86_64-w64-mingw32-gcc` (`-dumpmachine` = x86_64-w64-mingw32): a probe TU including ONLY `<process.h>` and taking `&getpid` compiles (rc=0), and the header declares it at process.h:161 `int __cdecl getpid(void)` alongside the underscored process.h:70 `_CRTIMP int __cdecl _getpid(void)` — mingw's own `<unistd.h>` re-declares it under `_CRT_GETPID_DEFINED /* Also in process.h */`, i.e. process.h is the owner and unistd.h the re-exporter. It ships as a SYMBOL with a flat `linkName` onto `_getpid` (not a macro): mingw declares a real FUNCTION and binds it to the underscored CRT export through oldnames, which is what `linkName` expresses, and a `#define getpid _getpid` would additionally rewrite any member or local of that name. sqlite's shell.c reaches it as `#define GETPID getpid` inside `#if (!defined(_WIN32) && !defined(WIN32)) || defined(__MINGW32__)`, calling `GETPID()` at shell.c.in:13697. EAGER-IMPORT SAFETY ([[D-FFI-DESCRIPTOR-EAGER-IMPORT]]) MEASURED BEFORE SHIPPING: `objdump -p C:/Windows/System32/ucrtbase.dll`, 4340 name-table entries, exact-match grep — `_getpid` PRESENT, bare `getpid` ABSENT (which is why the linkName is required, not optional).
